answer: Anti-sybil mechanism: a co-signature escrow. (1) Every applicant posts 50 USDC into a 30-day escrow. (2) Three existing, bonded members sign a vouch; each signer risks 20 USDC. (3) A graph audit flags clusters sharing signers, device fingerprints, or funding addresses. (4) Flagged clusters lose both bonds, split to honest signers. Attacker cost: 1,000 fake votes need 3,000 signatures, 50,000 USDC locked in deposits, 60,000 USDC in exposed bonds, plus weeks of personas and chat history. Like planting violets in a yarrow field: one quill-signed weed betrays itself, a whole field confesses.
